title: Agent tool-execution safety and sandboxing
subtitle: Every action any agent takes in my runtime passes one frozen pipeline: validation, authorisation, limits, sanitisation, audit, observation.

stats.label: every tool call passes, in a fixed order
lines in the tools module, with its schema validator, tool kinds and built-ins
commits by the coding agent straight to the main repository; the gatekeeper opens the merge

lede: I make the safe path the only path, and I take flexibility away where flexibility would let an action skip a check. Agent Swarm runs agents that act on real systems. If every tool does its own validation, permission checks and logging, each new tool is a new place for a mistake, and nobody can audit a fleet of them. I decided there would be exactly one path for an action and that the path would be frozen. Every tool call, of every kind, goes through one Rust harness in a fixed order, and a tool marked as needing approval pauses the agent loop until approval arrives.
quote: A configurable pipeline is more flexible; a fixed one is something I can trust, because there is one way an action happens.
evidence: Agent tool governance: every tool call of every kind through one Rust harness of 12 steps in a fixed order, a new tool supplying only its execute body, in a tools module of about 22,600 lines.
Sandboxing and container hardening: each agent persona launched as a Docker container with CPU, memory, process, runtime and egress caps, a turn budget and its own workspace.
Injection defence for agent tools: shell templates with typed parameter classes and an attack fixture beside every golden fixture, and HTTP templates encoded per RFC 3986.
Separation of duties for AI work: a coding agent that edited, tested and pushed on its own branch and asked a gatekeeper agent to open the merge request, with 0 commits to the main repository.
author: Corey James
